title: Enterprise-D Night Shift: public, tailnet-hosted browser game
description:
Outcome: a polished first-person browser game exploring the USS Enterprise-D, with walk/run movement and text chat at any time with the computer or crew. Hermes adds evolving dialogue and bounded story proposals; deterministic game code owns state and rules.

Canonical architecture and staged scope: docs/architecture/ADR-001.md. Preserve the full destination while keeping the first release to a small playable skeleton and vertical slice. Public fan-work uses original art only and does not imply IP rights.

Completion evidence: tested browser game; Hermes-disabled full playthrough; zero-tool Hermes profile verified before live calls; current-iOS real-device QA; tailnet-only live acceptance; exact pushed SHA with green CI; documented install/rollback and asset provenance.
acceptance_criteria: All milestone children satisfy their acceptance evidence; integrated game is playable and safe; exact public revision passes CI; tailnet service is read back and verified by an operator.

title: Stage 0–1: Tested skeleton and first playable slice
description: Build and verify the smallest useful game foundation: typed contracts, CI, one interior route, walk/run, interaction, persistent chat shell, deterministic offline dialogue, one short incident and save/reload. Do not start broad content production before this end-to-end slice is playable.
acceptance_criteria: A first-time player can enter the one-room route, move, interact, open/close chat without losing input state, resolve the authored incident, refresh, and see the committed outcome; tests pass.

title: Bootstrap the tested TypeScript monorepo and CI
description: Create the minimal Vite/React client, Fastify server, shared contracts/rules packages, package scripts, lint/typecheck/unit-test/build CI, lockfile, dependency automation, ignore rules, and public-project license baseline. Keep app code skeletal; no deployment credentials or provider secrets. CI must be read/test/package only.
acceptance_criteria: Frozen install, lint, typecheck, unit tests, and production build run locally and in CI; a deliberately failing unit test fails CI; no secrets are tracked.
close_reason: Acceptance verified: npm ci and npm run validate passed; unit tests and failure-propagation regression passed; browser chat smoke and live /health probe passed; PR #2 merged to master at e4271f199958a698675330aa4b926c6705ec25e4; exact-merge SHA CI run 39891772356 succeeded with no annotations; CI is read-only and no secrets are tracked.

title: Define versioned game, chat, and save contracts
description: Create typed, runtime-validated schemas for bootstrap snapshots, movement input, interactions, chat requests/results, narrative proposals, and committed world events. Include command IDs, per-save IDs, sequence/version fields, size bounds, and idempotency semantics. Keep shared files integration-owned.
acceptance_criteria: Schemas validate representative good/bad fixtures; client/server typecheck against the same package; unknown fields and oversized chat/proposal values fail closed.

title: Build the Babylon.js engine bootstrap and one greybox room
description: Add a self-contained client scene module that selects WebGPU before scene construction when supported and otherwise uses WebGL. Build a single original greybox corridor/room with readable lighting, collision geometry, resize/context-loss handling, and a clean teardown. No licensed art or broad deck build.
acceptance_criteria: A browser E2E smoke opens the room, verifies the selected renderer label/test hook, survives resize and reload, and records no console errors; WebGL remains force-testable.

title: Implement deterministic server-owned movement and interaction rules
description: Implement typed game state, bounded movement commands, simple swept corridor collision, interactable proximity/access checks, deterministic incident state transitions, and an append-only event record. No physics framework until measured need. Client-supplied coordinates or completion claims never grant rewards.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover collision boundaries, speed caps, access, command replay, stale versions, and reward-once behavior; domain code has no rendering or Hermes dependency.

title: Add landscape-first touch controls and always-available chat shell
description: Build a responsive HUD with left-thumb movement stick, right-thumb look drag, run toggle, contextual interact, and a persistent chat button. Handle independent pointer IDs, pointercancel, blur, chat open/close, safe areas, keyboard resize, portrait rotate hint, reduced motion, and keyboard/desktop controls.
acceptance_criteria: Playwright verifies movement releases on cancel/blur/chat-open, chat remains reachable in portrait and landscape, touch targets and safe-area layout fit, and desktop keyboard control remains usable.

title: Deliver the offline Night Watch vertical slice with save/reload
description: Integrate the first tiny route and one authored Night Watch EPS disturbance. Include the computer chat anywhere and one authored NPC conversation at proximity or over an explicit comm link; let the player inspect evidence, choose between two priorities, observe a server-committed consequence, and resume after reload. Keep the full loop playable without provider/Hermes configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Automated first-time playthrough reaches both outcome branches; computer chat opens anywhere and NPC chat follows its scope rule; saved outcome reloads correctly; provider-disabled play remains complete.

title: Add browser E2E and visual checks for the offline slice
description: Add a reproducible Playwright browser suite for the skeleton and offline incident. Cover desktop, landscape mobile viewport, portrait fallback, chat keyboard, rapid touch cancellation, reload, network/provider-disabled behavior, console errors, and initial visual baseline.
acceptance_criteria: CI installs browsers and runs deterministic E2E with no secrets; screenshots/artifacts are retained on failure; all visible controls in the first-slice inventory are exercised.

title: Add sequenced WebSocket movement and event transport
description: Implement the single real-time game channel after typed contracts and deterministic rules exist: bounded sequenced movement inputs, command IDs, server acknowledgements/state versions, authoritative events, chat-result events, rate/backpressure limits, reconnect snapshots, stale/duplicate rejection, and client prediction/interpolation reconciliation. Keep bootstrap/save/chat submission on HTTP where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover order, duplicate/lost messages, reconnect, stale versions, bounded queues, and client reconciliation; simulated latency does not freeze local movement and authoritative state converges.

title: Persist isolated saves and idempotent game events in SQLite
description: Implement single-host SQLite/WAL persistence with server-issued unguessable save capabilities, per-save ownership checks, transactionally committed choices/idempotency records, and a compact event history. Save at important actions and periodically; do not introduce an account system or broad event-sourcing framework. Keep recent walking loss on crash an explicit documented trade-off.
acceptance_criteria: Restart/refresh restores the correct save/outcome; cross-save reads and writes fail; duplicate mutation IDs commit once; transaction-interruption tests never report uncommitted success.

title: Stage 2: Isolated Hermes narrative and bounded world evolution
description: Add Hermes only behind a dedicated game profile and NarrativeBroker. Verify an empty effective tool registry and fail closed to authored responses otherwise. Model dialogue and event proposals as untrusted, typed, bounded data; game rules alone commit state.
acceptance_criteria: A real Hermes-backed chat run produces a validated response; malformed, stale, cross-save, or tool-bearing requests cannot mutate a save; provider-offline play remains complete.

title: Prove a dedicated Hermes game profile has zero effective tools
description: Design and test the deployment recipe for a separate game-only Hermes profile and key. Hermes API-server requests run with an empty effective tool registry; the standard hermes-api-server bundle is explicitly rejected because it retains host-capable tools. Verify configured tools through the supported server surface. If zero tools cannot be proven, keep live Hermes disabled and report the precise blocker.
acceptance_criteria: A real isolated-profile probe shows zero tools available to the model; hostile player text cannot invoke terminal/files/browser/MCP/delegation; profile/key are separate from operator default; failure returns the game to offline mode.

title: Validate bounded narrative replies and event proposals
description: Implement the game-owned validator for plain text and optional references to shipped incident templates. Bind proposals to one save, permitted entities, allowed state versions, prerequisites, resource costs, cooldowns, and solvability checks. Reject scripts, SQL, HTML, URLs, paths, arbitrary patches, stale or duplicate proposals.
acceptance_criteria: Adversarial fixtures for prompt injection, malformed JSON, oversized replies, cross-save IDs, stale state, invalid template/target, and duplicate proposal are rejected with no persisted mutation.

title: Add the Hermes NarrativeBroker with deadline and authored fallback
description: Implement the backend adapter to the dedicated Hermes endpoint without exposing its key to the browser. Use per-save bounded history/context, correlation/idempotency IDs, response deadlines, bounded concurrency/cost, cancellation, redacted errors, and a deterministic authored fallback. Never use the operator default profile.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test covers success, timeout, 429, invalid JSON, lost connection, duplicate submission, and save isolation; every failure leaves movement/gameplay available and returns valid fallback output.

title: Connect ship-computer and crew chat to save-scoped narrative state
description: Integrate the always-available computer chat and proximity/comm-link NPC conversations. Context includes only allow-listed current facts and a short bounded transcript. Persist chat, show pending/error/fallback status, and associate validated consequences with current state versions.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove chat can open at any time, speaker scope is enforced, refresh/reconnect does not duplicate turns, and model prose cannot claim a false authoritative fact or change the save directly.

title: Constrain the narrative worker with an OS-level least-authority boundary
description: Package the dedicated Hermes narrative runtime as an unprivileged, separately bounded service/process. Require read-only root, no host mounts or Docker socket, no host networking, minimal environment, bounded CPU/memory/processes/scratch, and only fixed-route inference egress. Keep game API key distinct from provider keys; provide a fail-closed local config and safe teardown notes.
acceptance_criteria: A runtime probe demonstrates the exact mount/network/UID/resource boundary; hostile player/model payload cannot access host files, tools, operator profile, arbitrary egress, or other saves; failed boundary checks disable Hermes and preserve authored dialogue.

title: Stage 3: Ship expansion, original content, and iPhone quality
description: Expand rooms, crew, incident families, visual fidelity, asset loading, and mobile controls in separately verifiable slices. Measure WebGPU/WebGL and any WASM candidate on named iPhones before promoting optional complexity.
acceptance_criteria: At least two outcome-dependent playthroughs span multiple locations; current iOS Safari landscape play is verified on device; performance targets are backed by measurements and a documented test method.

title: Establish original-asset provenance and fan-work policy
description: Add a source/rights inventory and project notice. Use original geometry, procedurally generated set dressing, and independently created interface art. Exclude franchise logos, extracted ship models, broadcast screenshots, music, fonts, and other unlicensed assets; identify every third-party dependency/license.
acceptance_criteria: Automated asset inventory and manual review find no undocumented media; README notice does not imply ownership or permission; every shipped asset has provenance.

title: Add a navigable Sickbay location
description: Create an original Sickbay zone with accessible navigation, a small number of meaningful medical-resource interactions, and a scene state that can visibly respond to mission outcomes. Avoid graphic content and ensure UI remains readable on a phone.
acceptance_criteria: Zone transition and resource rules are tested; each interaction is authoritative; visual outcome state survives reload and remains readable in mobile landscape.

title: Add a navigable Ten Forward social location
description: Create an original social space and ambient crew positioning that gives NPC conversations a clear place and purpose. Keep ambience lightweight; no copied set, music, or unlicensed fonts.
acceptance_criteria: At least one NPC schedule/conversation works there; ambient effects can be reduced; route/interaction tests pass and all assets have provenance.

title: Add a science laboratory location
description: Add an original science lab zone for diagnostic/investigation play with a distinct visual language and one evidence-gathering interaction. Do not make it a passive empty room.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence is server-validated and feeds at least one authored incident; zone route, save/reload, and mobile performance checks pass.

title: Add a shuttle-bay location
description: Add a bounded original shuttle-bay zone with navigation landmarks and one operational interaction that can be used in later mission content. Keep the initial asset and mesh budget explicit.
acceptance_criteria: Zone is streamable and traversable on the reference phone, contains no dead-end softlock, and any operation is validated by server rules.

title: Add one crew-quarters location
description: Add a compact, original crew-quarters area to make the interior feel inhabited while avoiding individualized private-life simulation. Provide one benign inspect/conversation hook for later story content.
acceptance_criteria: Zone loads/unloads and can be left from every spawn/interaction state; visual and privacy boundaries are documented; provenance is complete.

title: Add an Observation Lounge location
description: Add an original Observation Lounge with a calm view treatment, accessible visual contrast, and a mission debrief/follow-up conversation hook. Do not use real episode imagery or audio.
acceptance_criteria: Entry/exit, conversation, debrief state and low-quality mode pass tests; no authored outcome is presented unless the server committed it.

title: Connect zones with a bounded turbolift and corridor route graph
description: Connect accepted locations with an explicit server-validated route graph, short transitions, safe respawn points, and neighboring-zone loading. Loading screens must not conceal a broken route or reset mission state.
acceptance_criteria: Every planned location is reachable and escapable, invalid destinations reject, save/reload preserves location safely, and p95 transition/load metrics are recorded.

title: Add deterministic crew schedules and conversation availability
description: Add small server-owned crew schedules and proximity/comm-link availability for the initial conversational crew. Persist seeds and state versions so NPC presence is testable; never let dialogue choose a crew member or reveal another save.
acceptance_criteria: Schedule replay is deterministic; player can always reach computer chat; NPC scope is enforced; disconnect/reload does not duplicate schedule events or chat turns.

title: Add a medical-capacity incident with two valid resolutions
description: Create an original, deterministic follow-up incident that uses Engineering and Sickbay resources, has two feasible strategies, and reflects prior Night Watch consequences. Hermes may enrich text but cannot alter requirements or outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Both paths pass solvability/property tests; each produces visible, persisted consequences and a valid follow-up; Hermes-disabled play remains complete.

title: Add a sensor-integrity incident with evidence-based outcomes
description: Create an original bridge/science-lab investigation where evidence, NPC reports, and instrument data can disagree; permit multiple evidence-based resolutions and carry a server-owned consequence forward.
acceptance_criteria: Tests verify evidence/access rules, seeded replay, two solvable branches, reload, and that generated prose cannot fabricate evidence or claim an uncommitted choice.

title: Build the modular interior zone kit and loading boundaries
description: Implement the reusable original-geometry zone contract: spawn/exit points, collision bounds, interactable placement, visibility/loading boundaries, and repeatable test fixtures. This bead is infrastructure only; add ship locations in their own beads so one large room pack cannot hide regressions. Keep the 10–12-space destination from ADR-001 visible without building it in one pass.
acceptance_criteria: Two small original test zones load/unload without leaks or softlocks; crossing a boundary keeps controls responsive; zone geometry/metadata have deterministic validation and payload measurements.

title: Add crew trust, qualifications, and outcome-dependent assignments
description: Implement a narrow server-owned progression path from incident outcomes: qualification, access unlock, crew trust, and a follow-up assignment. Avoid arbitrary stat inflation and make every unlock observable in conversation or interaction.
acceptance_criteria: Two complete playthroughs produce visibly different follow-ups; unlocks survive reload, are awarded once, and cannot be forged by client or model output.

title: Build deterministic mission templates and solvability checks
description: Implement server-owned mission definitions, eligibility, prerequisites, costs, cooldowns, outcome transitions, and seeded variation. Keep this rules layer deterministic and usable with Hermes disabled. Model proposals may reference only shipped templates; do not let the narrative system invent actions or arbitrary patches. See ADR-001.
acceptance_criteria: Property tests show every published template is reachable and resource-feasible; invalid, stale, duplicate, or cross-save state changes are rejected; deterministic replay yields the same outcome for a saved seed.

title: Verify the game on a real iPhone running current iOS Safari
description: Run device QA on the latest public iOS release available at execution time; current planning baseline is iOS 27.0.1 (2026-10-16). Test landscape, rotation, multitouch, software keyboard, safe areas, WebGL fallback, WebGPU where available, context loss, background/resume, and 10-minute thermal behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Attach device/model/iOS/Safari versions, reproducible cases, videos or screenshots, FPS/frame-time and memory samples; all blocker defects fixed or explicitly accepted. Browser emulation alone does not pass.

title: Measure and optimize asset loading and frame-time budgets
description: Establish named reference-device profiling. Measure cold load, compressed payload, frame-time distribution, memory, input latency, and repeated zone transitions. Use zones, compressed textures, instancing, baked lighting, and quality tiers only where measurements justify them.
acceptance_criteria: A 10-minute reference-device report shows p95 frame-time <=34 ms with 30 FPS floor, initial compressed payload <=8 MiB, and interactive <=6 seconds on the documented 20 Mbps/100 ms link; results are measured, not inferred.

title: Run a bounded WebGPU/WASM physics and CPU-hotspot experiment
description: Time-box a benchmark comparing the current deterministic TypeScript movement/collision path with an isolated WASM candidate; separately record renderer performance with WebGPU and WebGL. Adopt WASM only if it materially improves a measured target-device bottleneck without worsening startup, memory, accessibility, or testability.
acceptance_criteria: Publish reproducible device/browser/build inputs, measurements, bundle/memory cost, and a go/no-go decision. No WASM physics enters production merely because it is fashionable.

title: Create an original modular interior art and lighting kit
description: Develop a coherent original visual language for ship interiors: reusable bulkheads, doors, consoles, deck markings, signs, restrained animated lighting, and accessible contrast. Use procedural geometry or assets with documented provenance; do not reproduce protected logos, screenshots, models, music, fonts, or extracted set designs.
acceptance_criteria: A representative corridor/console looks polished at mobile landscape resolution, holds text/interaction contrast in low and bright scenes, supports low-quality settings, and every source asset is inventoried with provenance.

title: Add the first modular Engineering location
description: Create an independently loadable, original Engineering area using the shared zone and art kits. Include clear navigation landmarks, one useful repair interaction, and collision that respects the walkable route. Keep geometry and metadata under a zone-owned directory; use the shared registry only through the integration owner.
acceptance_criteria: Entry/exit, collision, one interaction, reload, low-quality rendering, and mobile traversal pass automated checks; payload is measured and no player can become softlocked.

title: Add a navigable Bridge location
description: Create an original, readable Bridge zone using modular assets. Include operational stations with server-authoritative interactions and sightlines that make the room legible without copying broadcast frames or exact proprietary graphics.
acceptance_criteria: Zone transitions and station access rules are tested; mobile frame/payload budgets are recorded; assets have provenance and no missing/overlapping collider blocks the route.

title: Stage 4: Tailnet operations and public release
description: Package an operator-run, tailnet-only deployment with localhost service binding, Tailscale Serve, health checks, backups and restore instructions. Public CI may test/package but must never have host deployment credentials.
acceptance_criteria: The exact public commit passes CI; operator deployment is reachable only through the tailnet; health, game save, Hermes chat, backup and restore are read back successfully.

title: Package a localhost-only tailnet deployment
description: Add operator-run deployment assets: user systemd unit/container choice, explicit loopback binding, Tailscale Serve path, environment file templates, health checks, restart/rollback, and no GitHub Actions server credentials. Verify ports and target ownership before installation.
acceptance_criteria: Service works locally; Hermes endpoint is not browser-exposed; Tailscale Serve maps only the intended path; live health/game/chat are read back over a logged-in tailnet; rollback is documented.

title: Unblock deployment by authenticating the host to its tailnet
description: Tailnet access is an operator-controlled deployment prerequisite. Do not run tailscale up, login, ACL, or key changes without explicit operator approval. Once the operator confirms tailnet access, verify service routing and exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Operator-authenticated tailnet state is read back; health is reachable from an authorized peer and not from public internet; exact approved Serve path and node name are recorded.
notes: Awaiting operator-controlled tailnet authentication; no credentials, host details, or ACL changes are recorded here.

title: Add backup and restore for game saves and event history
description: Document and implement consistent SQLite/WAL backup, retention, integrity checks, restore procedure, and a tested recovery point for saves, events, and narrative correlation. Keep secrets and provider transcripts out of backups unless explicitly needed.
acceptance_criteria: Automated restore test recovers a save with correct mission outcome/idempotency state; backup integrity is verified; recovery-point/recovery-time limits and exclusions are documented.

title: Qualify and publish a reproducible public release
description: Finish README, contribution/security/reporting docs, dependency automation, CI pins, license/provenance, artifact packaging, and an exact-SHA release checklist. CI can build and attach artifacts but has no server deploy or tailnet privileges.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh clone can run the documented local/offline path; all CI gates pass on the exact pushed SHA; dependency audit and asset provenance pass; release notes state current device/test limits and no unverified performance claims.
